reason: The file writes a second `<body>` after content has already opened one. HTML5 tree construction merges that start tag's attributes into the body already open and creates no node, which parse5 does and scylla does not: scylla's markup tree is a lossless tiling of the bytes, so every start tag written becomes an element. The rest of the file's 3,000 elements agree.

The file renders C++ source into HTML, so `#include <vulkan/vulkan_core.h>` reads as a tag. HTML5 ends a tag name at `/` and then reconsumes in the before-attribute-name state, which makes `vulkan_core.h` the attribute; scylla keeps the `/` on the front of the attribute name, since a bare `/` inside a tag carries no token of its own in a lossless tiling. Every other name in the file agrees.
